analysis:
Examined the InferenceHandler head excerpt (lines ~1144-1560) and the ModelLoading patch/base. InferenceHandler: the deadline gate now keys on v2UsageSignal.firstWithheldOutputAt (replacing firstWithheldReasoningAt), so withheld answer text also counts as generated output. firstContentElapsedMs uses that timestamp. Added GLM5NextWiredLimitNotice.report calls in error paths (patch lines 577, 1023; head line 1325). These are diagnostics only, and I saw no plaintext exposure in what was supplied. Response hashing (fullResponseText), SE-signed attestation, cache usage fields (gated on remoteCache.scope), and the terminal-finalization paths are unchanged in structure. Residual question: if withheld answer text is excluded from fullResponseText, the response-hash domain could diverge from emitted bytes (T-007/TB-007). That depends on code outside the supplied excerpts and is not provable here.

ModelLoading: weight hashing is routed through an injectable `loadWeightHasher` closure. Its definition and default are not in the supplied units, so production binding to WeightHasher.computeHash is unverified (T-012/T-027/T-041 weight-hash binding for the SSD cache). For GLM plans, the pre/post-load captureWeightHash passes are replaced by verifiedGLM5NextWeightHash(load:plan:modelPath:). It passes the same verified digest as both preLoad and postLoad to finalizeReusableSSDLoad, so the TOCTOU 'changed' comparison is trivially equal. Protection now depends on the managed load's per-file SHA-256 manifest verification, file-identity snapshots (identitiesBeforeLoad) and recordVerifiedGLM5NextWeightHash, none of which are visible. The removed requireGLM5NextLoadedArtifact check is presumably subsumed by this. A new fail-closed throw (managedLoadRequired) guards the impossible nil-preLoadHash case. The non-GLM paths are logically preserved. Next pass should check GLM5NextManagedLoad, verifiedGLM5NextWeightHash, the loadWeightHasher default, and the firstWithheldOutputAt producer. No concrete regression is established from the supplied evidence.
